_readme: Skin colours for raceforge.py skins. Each race (found by its client_file_string in races.json, at its realm_id) gets the textures of its CharSections rows of the listed sections recoloured into new files under Character\BleakholdSkins\<ClientFileString>\, and only its rows point at them: the template race's textures and rows stay as they are. Sections: 0 skin, 1 face, 4 underwear (a row's colour index is the skin colour in these three; hair and facial hair are never recoloured). Underwear is left out by default: its cloth colours sit near skin hues and would turn purple too; but an opaque underwear texture (the package's NakedPelvis/NakedTorso: the skin with the garment painted in) is recoloured where it is bare skin whenever section 0 is, so a purple skin never shows the template's skin through it (README.md, Skins). palette: the target colours, lightest first; the race's skin colours of a sex are ranked by lightness and spread over it (OKLab). dk_palette: the same for the Death Knight rows (flag 0x4). transform: how far each colour of a texture moves, see README.md (Skins). An empty sections list puts every row back on its original textures.

races.comment: Night-elf-like purple from pale lavender to deep violet (an OKLab ramp, a little more colourful in the middle), replacing the fair Blood Elf skin; Death Knights a desaturated grey-violet.

transform.comment: Tuned on previews of made-up elf skin textures: hue_spread 0.3 and chroma_max 0.16 (not 0.6 and 0.25) keep lips and shadows violet instead of a bright blue; chroma_floor 0.02 (not 0.005) keeps a nearly grey Death Knight skin from colourful speckles.
